name: 14377-multiimage-qwen2vl7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration, bf16, 8.3B: a 32-block vision tower (patch 14, 2x2 merge) feeding a 28-layer decoder, hidden 3584, 4 KV heads, 32768-token window.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=100, bounded at 3000 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, warmup the first 30% by completion. `max-num-seqs: 1` pins the engine to one request per step, so the offered load is a hundred clients deep while a step is one client's four photographs.
workload: Real image+text chat: FOUR distinct photographs and four short questions in ONE turn, one token out (`max_tokens: 1`, `temperature: 0.0`). Four `huggingface` sources over disjoint row ranges of `merve/vqav2-small` (validation [0:5000], [5000:10000], [10000:15000], [15000:20000]) put four pictures and four questions in one request; rows are consumed in order and never repeat inside a 3000-request run. Every photograph is served at THUMBNAIL size -- `mm-processor-kwargs: {"max_pixels": 78400}`, at most 100 merged tokens and ~368 encoder patches apiece -- so a median request is ~406 prompt tokens over ~1472 encoder patches, worst case ~426 tokens, measured over 12 rows of the declared slices. The pictures are ~98% of every prompt. `request_format: plain` with `image_placeholder: <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>`: the prompt is built directly rather than through the tokenizer's chat template, because this engine's `AsyncLLMEngine` exposes no `.tokenizer` for the client to template with, and the placeholder is spelled exactly as that template would have spelled it, so the engine's processor sees the same four image spans and the prompt differs only by the absent role scaffolding.
purpose: A visual question-answering assistant comparing four thumbnail photos per turn for a hundred concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
model: Qwen/Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct

# Four images per request is the workload, and the engine default is ONE per modality per
# prompt: without this line every request is rejected before it reaches the engine.
# MUST STAY INLINE JSON ON ONE LINE -- the config reader is line-based and skips every line
# starting with a space, so a block-form dict silently never reaches the engine.
limit-mm-per-prompt: {"image": 4}

tensor-parallel-size: 1

# Each photograph is served at THUMBNAIL size: at most 78400 pixels, i.e. 100 merged image
# tokens and ~368 encoder patches apiece. A four-photograph request is then ~406 prompt tokens
# instead of ~1438. Measured over 12 rows of the declared slices, not estimated.
# MUST STAY INLINE JSON ON ONE LINE -- same line-based reader hazard as limit-mm-per-prompt.
mm-processor-kwargs: {"max_pixels": 78400}

# One request per prefill step, so a step is exactly one client's four photographs. The hundred
# clients still queue; the batch composition is pinned, the offered load is not.
max-num-seqs: 1

# Comfortably above the declared workload, whose worst case is now well under 700 tokens; the
# checkpoint's own 32768 window would reserve KV this item never touches.
max-model-len: 4096
